title: Predictive mixed longitudinal-transverse intermittency exponents
statement: Develop a predictive description of the mixed longitudinal-transverse structure-function exponents in statistically stationary homogeneous isotropic incompressible turbulence, consistent with exact moment relations and the connection between inertial-range increments and dissipative-range gradients. State moment conventions, scaling ranges and the Reynolds-number limit.
source_locator: Buaria, Physical Review Fluids 11 L092601, conclusions pp.6-7 and Appendix C; Buaria and Pumir, section 9.1.
status_basis: The September 2026 published paper retains the missing full mixed-exponent description; the review identifies the same need. Targeted searches found no later complete resolution.
plain_summary: Rare intense fluctuations govern turbulent mixing and dissipation. Their longitudinal and transverse statistics need a joint predictive account rather than separate fitted scaling curves.
assumptions: Three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes dynamics; specify forcing, stationarity, homogeneity and isotropy.

For separation r e, let delta u_L=[u(x+r e)-u(x)] dot e and delta u_T be one perpendicular component. Define absolute mixed moments S_p,q(r)=E[|delta u_L|^p |delta u_T|^q] for nonnegative orders with finite moments, and their inertial-range exponents by S_p,q(r)~r^zeta_p,q. Signed moments have separate conventions and may vanish by symmetry.
State the inertial-range and high-Reynolds-number assumptions; identify any additional closure or multifractal hypothesis.
scope: A statistical prediction problem for mixed velocity increments and gradients; not a proof of Navier-Stokes global regularity.
target: An explicit predictive account of the mixed-exponent family, or a clearly delimited partial result.
success_criteria: Define which moments and parameter range the result covers, including symmetry-forced zero moments.
Recover the applicable signed third-moment identities without substituting absolute moments for them; distinguish proved relations from modeled closures.
For empirical claims, compare independent statistics with uncertainty and finite-Reynolds-number controls.
known_results: Buaria provides a joint multifractal framework linking increment and gradient statistics, without closing the entire exponent family.
Published equations (18)-(19) use the 4/5 and one-transverse-component 4/15 relations; the earlier preprint's 4/3 wording should not be copied.
The paper notes that further changes of exponents at much higher Reynolds numbers cannot be excluded.
prerequisites: Incompressible turbulence, structure functions and multifractal modeling.
Statistical convergence, Reynolds-number scaling and numerical resolution.
significance: A reliable theory would clarify extreme-event statistics relevant to dissipation, mixing and transport. Any improvement to reduced fluid models needs separate demonstration.

requirements.experiment: No new experiment is required for analytical work. Empirical validation requires suitable numerical or measured evidence.
requirements.data: The cited DNS data are available upon reasonable request and were not publicly deposited; access has not been obtained.
requirements.compute: Symbolic checks and analysis of selected statistics may be modest; new well-resolved high-Reynolds-number DNS is a major computing task. No costs or runtimes are measured.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: The declared flow class, moment definitions, scaling limit and any statistical closure must remain explicit.

obstacles: Finite scaling windows can imitate asymptotic exponents.
Model assumptions can be mistaken for consequences of Navier-Stokes dynamics.

steps: Check increment conventions and exact low-order identities against the published version.
List each additional statistical hypothesis and where it enters.
Separate fitting data from validation data and examine resolution, sampling, anisotropy and scaling-window sensitivity.
Retain uncertainty and alternative extrapolations rather than certifying universality from finite data.
validation.human_review_difficulty: High: statistical and fluid-dynamical assumptions require specialist assessment.
validation.statement_alignment: A successful fit or conditional closure is not a general derivation of turbulence exponents.

known_attempts: The cited articles report theoretical frameworks and numerical comparisons; this project has not reproduced them.
unresolved_checks: Confirm access, rights and suitability of any validation data.
A low-order subproblem is Curator-proposed; pending review and a focused novelty check.
